section_1.title: Prerequisite Review: The Static Slope
section_1.content: Briefly revisit the standard definition of a derivative as the 'slope of a tangent line' at a specific point x. Visualize a static curve where the tangent line is a fixed ruler resting on a point.
section_1.example: A hiker standing still on a mountain path; the slope of the ground under their feet represents the derivative at that specific location.

section_2.title: The Shift: Derivative as a Transformation
section_2.content: Introduce the 'Transformational View'. Instead of viewing the derivative as a single number, view it as a function that maps the input space (x) to the output space (f'(x)). Use animation to show the 'speedometer' of the function changing as we slide across the domain.
section_2.example: A robotic arm tracing a curve; the derivative acts as the 'steering command' that transforms the arm's velocity vector based on its current position.

section_3.title: Visualizing the Mapping (The Derivative Machine)
section_3.content: Use a split-screen animation: Left side shows the function f(x) and a moving point; Right side shows the derivative function f'(x) tracing its own path simultaneously. This reinforces that the derivative 'transforms' input curvature into output height.
section_3.example: A chameleon catching a fly: The chameleon's tongue speed (f'(x)) is mapped against its position relative to the fly (x), showing how the 'transformation' adjusts as it gets closer.

section_4.title: Synthesis and Intuition
section_4.content: Summarize that derivatives are not just numbers, but 'operators' that tell us how the function warps or stretches the input. This perspective prepares students for multivariable calculus and linear algebra.
section_4.example: A digital image filter: Think of the derivative as a 'gradient filter' that transforms a smooth image into an outline by detecting the rate of change in pixel intensity.

import numpy as np

        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Map to right side of screen: x > 0
                x = 2.0 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
